papers.authors: N Zhou, W Luo, Z Wu, Y Du, K Shi, B Chen - Applied Intelligence, 2026
papers.abstract: Graph-regularized representation methods have demonstrated promising performance in image clustering. papers.title: Image dehazing with an-regularized extreme channels prior
papers.authors: H Zhao, H Xu - Pattern Analysis and Applications, 2026
papers.abstract: Current challenges in image dehazing are mostly related to scene variability, including darkened images and distortions caused by non-uniform fog density, atmospheric variability, and depth differences. This paper proposes a novel approach to address these issues by integrating Extreme Channels Prior (ECP) into restoration models. Specifically, an norm constraint is applied to the extreme channel values, which effectively guides the iterative restoration process towards a haze-free …

papers.title: Block Coordinate Dinkelbach Algorithms for Solving Block-Structured Constrained Fractional Optimization Problems
papers.authors: C Ennouri, K Boufi, A Roubi - Operations Research Forum, 2026
papers.abstract: In this paper, we are interested in solving optimization programs whose objective function is expressed as the ratio of two real-valued functions, with block-separable constraints. This kind of problems is difficult due to a possible lack of convexity and is more difficult in the case of large sizes. For this, we propose two algorithms that are based on the block coordinate method: Dinkelbach and the proximal point algorithms. papers.abstract: Convolutive non-negative matrix factorization has been a dominant analytical technique for deriving interpretable insights from data in speech processing, image analysis, data mining, biomedicine, and other fields. papers.title: ADMM-Based Approach for a Class of Composite Function Optimization Problems
papers.abstract: In this study, we optimize a class of composite function problems whose objective function is a sum of three terms: a smooth function, a simple convex function, and a composite function composed of a simple convex function and a linear function. This kind of problem is challenging to solve, as the last two functions are both non-smooth and non-separable. papers.title: An Information-Theoretic Approach to Machine Learning Privacy and Security
papers.abstract: Abstract Machine learning models are vulnerable to a wide array of security attacks (eg, adversarial examples) and privacy attacks (eg, membership inference, data reconstruction). Existing defenses are often attack-specific, sacrifice significant utility, or are broken by adaptive adversaries, necessitating a more principled approach.
